title: Metrics Start With a Behaviour Model
editorial_note: Automated dialogue draft from the revised lesson. Review spoken wording and meaning before publishing.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Today we're talking about Metrics Start With a Behaviour Model. By the end, you'll know why this matters, how to use it, and what to notice in a real product.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the problem we are trying to understand?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A metric is a defined quantitative summary. A behavioural model explains why a change in that measure might represent value. Without the model, teams optimise what is easy to log.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at metrics operationalise a theory?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Write the causal chain in plain language:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: In situation, a person or actor encounters condition, interprets it as meaning, takes action, receives system or service response, and reaches near-term result, which contributes to longer-term outcome.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Then add competing paths, friction, recovery, and external factors. Product telemetry observes only parts of this chain. A click records an interaction, not the person’s motivation, comprehension, or benefit. Operational records may reveal fulfilment. Interviews or surveys may reveal interpretation. Outcomes may occur days later or outside the product.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A good model distinguishes four layers:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: exposure: the person had a credible opportunity to experience the change; behaviour: they acted, avoided, repeated, or recovered; service result: the system and people fulfilled or failed the request; outcome: the person made meaningful progress.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Define the measure so it can be challenged
turns.text: What changes when we look at define the measure so it can be challenged?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: For every metric specify:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: construct being approximated; event or source and exact trigger; unit of analysis—event, session, patient, referral, clinic, or household; eligible population and denominator; inclusion and exclusion rules; identity and cross-device logic; time window and attribution window; deduplication, retries, missing data, and late-arriving events; properties required for segmentation; owner, version, and quality tests.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: “Conversion rate” is not a complete definition. Referral booking conversion might mean unique eligible referrals with a confirmed appointment within fourteen days divided by referrals shown at least one feasible option. Changing the denominator to all created referrals answers a different question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: daily active users?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Daily activity can rise because a messaging product is valuable, notifications are manipulative, a workflow is confusing, or failures cause repeated opening. A behavioural model asks which action produces user value, whether a successful session occurred, and what downstream evidence should follow. “Users opened the app” is exposure or activity, not proof of benefit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Test the model, not just the feature
turns.text: What changes when we look at test the model, not just the feature?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: After release, inspect whether links in the chain move together. If explanation views rise but correct understanding does not, exposure is not comprehension. If reservations rise while clinic acceptance falls, local conversion is damaging service quality. If accepted appointments rise only for digitally confident patients, the aggregate hides inequity.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Update the model when evidence contradicts it. Measurement is not a scoreboard added after design; it is a way to test the team’s theory of value.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at where this can go wrong?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Available-event metric: instrumentation dictates strategy. Proxy collapse: an action is treated as the outcome it approximates. Undefined denominator: rates change because eligible populations differ. State compression: request, pending, confirmation, and fulfilment share one misleading event.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Competing-explanation blindness: movement is attributed to the feature without checking context. Instrumentation drift: a release changes event meaning without versioning the metric.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Connect product behavior to human and service outcomes
turns.text: What changes when we look at connect product behavior to human and service outcomes?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: He distinguishes user behavior, system state, service operation, and outcome. Repeated status checks may signal engagement, confusion, delayed processing, or a high-stakes task. The model predicts which supporting measures can separate those explanations: state latency, comprehension research, support contacts, duplicate actions, and unresolved cases.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The team marks what instrumentation can and cannot observe, who is missing, and where privacy limits collection. Qualitative evidence tests the mechanism; operational and product data estimate pattern and change. Metrics are revised when the behavior model is disproved. This prevents an available dashboard event from becoming the definition of success.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Metrics create incentives. Once a number becomes a target, teams discover ways to move it that may weaken the construct it represented. Senior designers participate in measurement design because event semantics encode the service model. They ask whose behaviour is observable, whose outcome is missing, and what labour or harm the dashboard excludes.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Treat sensitive health data with purpose limitation, access controls, retention rules, and aggregation appropriate to risk. Do not collect a property merely because future analysis might be interesting. A trustworthy measurement system is selective as well as detailed.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: a learning app. “More sessions” sounds like success until the team maps the desired behaviour: learners practise a skill, get useful feedback, return when they need it, and improve. Session count is an input signal at best.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The model identifies the meaningful outcome, intermediate behaviours, and places where the product could increase activity without increasing learning.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Find a dashboard headline. Ask what human behaviour and outcome it claims to represent. Identify one repeated action, failed state, or population change that could move the number without increasing value.
